implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX and exactly ONE ordinary stack argument, the out-record pointer at entry+4. The one slot is machine-observed: 0x006417f4 `MOV ECX,[ESP+0x8]` is read with ESP at entry-4, so entry-4+0x8 = entry+4, and it is the word the body then stores through at 0x006417f8 and 0x006417fd. The machine-derived ABI record lists one slot (entry_ESP+0x4) but marks it read:false; that is a walk artefact, and the record's own abstained_because lists "flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at -4, so the listing is not one path". The model reads the slot and the model test confirms the writes land in the caller's buffer.
implementation.return_note: a BYTE, not a word. 0x00641800 is `MOV AL,0x1` (B0 01) and 0x00641806 is `XOR AL,AL` (32 C0); neither writes the upper three bytes of EAX. Those three bytes carry the second copied dword on the true path (0x006417fa), the caller's own EAX on the 0x006417d8 exit and `inner+0x18` on the 0x006417e8 exit, so the three exits leave three different dead values there. All seven references to this body are DATA references from .rdata, so no caller in this image constrains them. The model test records the full EAX at every call site, asserts nothing above the low byte, and pins the declared type with a static_assert so a widening back to uint32_t cannot pass.
implementation.receiver_model: a struct whose only named member is the word at +0x1c, typed as a pointer to the inner object, with an opaque 0x1c run before it and an opaque 8-byte run after it. The body reads that word twice (0x006417d3 and 0x006417ea) and no other displacement, and stores nothing anywhere, so nothing else is named. The dispatch word at +0x00 is deliberately NOT declared even though the body is installed at slot 11 of six tables: the 23 instructions contain no LEA, no ADD and no displacement-free read of the receiver's leading word, so nothing here reads a vptr.
implementation.dispatch_model: no dispatch at all. abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, and the body contains no register- or memory-operand transfer. Both transfers are direct CALL rel32 to 0x005507a0, and the model makes them as ordinary C++ calls to a declared extern, so the instruction form is not altered to suit the test.
implementation.dependency_note: one direct callee, 0x005507a0, declared in the header and defined only by the model test as a five-load assembly trampoline plus a C++ body of the same __thiscall shape. The test also defines a cdecl probe that is never referenced by the model; it exists only so the RET 0x4 measurement can be shown to discriminate.

ECX is not changed by that move, so the first accessor call at 0x006417da still carries the word loaded at 0x006417d3; 0x006417ea reloads the word rather than trusting the register, because a callee is free to destroy ECX and because the instruction is a load.

observed_original_abi.frame: the body's only stack effect is `PUSH ESI` at 0x006417d0 and the two matching POP ESI. observed_original_abi.callee_conventions: 0x005507a0 is __thiscall by its own seventeen bytes: the first argument arrives in ECX, it is parked with `PUSH ECX; MOV [EBP-0x4],ECX`, the terminator is the one-byte C3 with no immediate, and EBP is saved and restored. The model test observes it through a trampoline that reads the callee's own entry stack frame, so the convention is measured at the callee rather than assumed from the caller's side.

mechanics.body_shape: alias the receiver into ESI; load the word at receiver+0x1c and require it non-zero; call 0x005507a0 on it and reject the result if BOTH of its two dwords are 0xffffffff; reload the word at receiver+0x1c, call 0x005507a0 a second time, and copy that result's two dwords into the caller's out record; return 1. Otherwise return 0 without writing anything. Two direct calls, no dispatch, no store except the two four-byte out-record stores, no global.

frame_resolution.method: the body pushes only ESI, never an argument, and never adjusts ESP, so ESP is at entry-4 from 0x006417d1 to the POP. 0x006417f4's `[ESP+0x8]` is therefore entry+4. The two `RET 0x4` terminators then consume the return address plus that one word, which is the machine half of stack_cleanup_bytes 4 / side callee.
frame_resolution.corroboration: the machine-derived ABI record independently reports ret_form "RET 0x4", stack_cleanup_bytes 4, stack_cleanup_owner "callee", saved_registers ["ESI"], one observed stack slot at entry_ESP+0x4 and ret_form-compatible return_register EAX. The model test measures the cleanup side rather than trusting the record: the caller's ESP must come back LEVEL after re_006417d0 and four bytes LOWER after a cdecl probe called through the same asm block.

slots.entry-4: the saved ESI, parked by 0x006417d0 PUSH ESI and given back by the POP at 0x00641802 (true path) or 0x00641808 (false block). Not a parameter and not a return value: both terminators are `RET 0x4`.
slots.entry+4: the one ordinary stack argument, the out-record pointer, read at 0x006417f4 and written through at 0x006417f8 and 0x006417fd.

receiver_displacement.0x1c: read twice, at 0x006417d3 and again at 0x006417ea. It is a LOAD of a word that is then used as a receiver (0x005507a0's first act is `MOV [EBP-0x4],ECX` followed by `ADD EAX,0x18` on it), so it is a pointer, and it is declared as one. The two reads are independent loads with a CALL between them and nothing else, so the second call's receiver is the word as the first callee left it. The model performs two loads; the model test proves the difference by having the first call rewrite the word and requiring the second call to see the new value.

mechanics.receiver_writes: none. The 23 instructions contain no store to memory whose destination is ESI-relative; the only two stores are 0x006417f8 and 0x006417fd, both through the stack argument. The model writes nothing on the receiver and the model test asserts a byte-for-byte match of the receiver block around every run.
mechanics.inner_object_writes: none either. The body reads the two dwords 0x005507a0 returns and stores them somewhere else; the model test snapshots the inner object and compares.
mechanics.dereference_depth: one level for the receiver word, one level below the returned pointer for the record. 0x006417d3 is a single load of a word used as a pointer, and 0x006417df/0x006417e4/0x006417f2/0x006417fa read through the pointer 0x005507a0 returned without ever loading a word out of it and using that as a pointer again. The model test plants a decoy word at the inner object's own +0x00 and live decoy observers at eight other receiver displacements, so a two-level receiver read or a wrong displacement calls something.
mechanics.accessor_addend: 0x18, and it belongs to the CALLEE. 0x005507a0's seventeen bytes are `55 8b ec 51 89 4d fc 8b 45 fc 83 c0 18 8b e5 5d c3`, i.e. PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ESP; PUSH ECX; MOV [EBP-0x4],ECX; MOV EAX,[EBP-0x4]; ADD EAX,0x18; MOV ESP,EBP; POP EBP; RET. The body adds nothing to the returned pointer, and the model test proves it: the observer returns a scripted record that is NOT at inner+0x18 while inner+0x00..+0x1c hold poison, so a model that hand-rolled the addend would copy kDecoy2.
mechanics.sentinel: the exact 32-bit pattern 0xffffffff, compared for equality, in BOTH words, as a conjunction. 0x006417df `CMP DWORD PTR [EAX],0xffffffff` (83 38 ff) branches AROUND 0x006417e4 when the first word is anything else, so the second compare is only reached on the first-word-is-sentinel path, and 0x006417e8 rejects only when the second word is also 0xffffffff. It is 32-bit equality, so there is no signed or unsigned question AT THIS COMPARE; the model test drives (0x80000000, 0xffffffff), (0xdeadbeef, 0xffffffff), (0xfffffffe, 0xffffffff), (0x7fffffff, 0xffffffff) and the 0x0000ffff / 0x0000fffe pair so that a signed compare, an unsigned band test and a 16-bit-truncated compare are each killed.
mechanics.short_circuit_is_a_pointer_level_fact: 0x006417e4 reads the probe's second dword ONLY when its first dword is the sentinel, so on every other path those four bytes are never touched. The model test places the probe four bytes before a PROT_NONE guard page, with a non-sentinel first word, and a model that read the second word unconditionally would fault.
mechanics.control_flow: three conditional branches, all Jcc, all with targets inside the recovered span: 0x006417d8 JZ 0x00641806 (the null receiver word), 0x006417e2 JNZ 0x006417ea (the first word is not the sentinel), 0x006417e8 JZ 0x00641806 (both words are). Five basic blocks: 0x006417d0..0x006417d8, 0x006417da..0x006417e2, 0x006417e4..0x006417e8, 0x006417ea..0x00641803 and the shared false block 0x00641806..0x00641809. The two false exits share one block, which is why the model has one false return.
mechanics.which_call_is_which: the FIRST call (0x006417da) produces the pair the sentinel test judges; the SECOND (0x006417ed) produces the pair that is copied. Nothing carries a value from one to the other. The model test makes this unambiguous by scripting a clean first pair and a sentinel second pair and requiring 1 with a sentinel written to the out record.
mechanics.not_modelled: the identity and meaning of the two dwords; the class of the object at receiver+0x1c; whether any real callee ever changes the receiver's +0x1c word; the upper three bytes of EAX; and the order of the two stores to the out record, which nothing in the 23 instructions can make observable.
mechanics.globals: none. No instruction in the body names a data-segment address, and the model names none.

direct_call_1.convention: __thiscall, receiver in ECX, no stack argument, callee-saved EBP, ECX preserved. Fixed by the callee's own seventeen bytes and its one-byte C3 terminator, and observed by the model test's trampoline as a frame containing only a return address.
direct_call_1.arguments: ECX, and nothing else. The word loaded at 0x006417d3 is still in ECX because nothing between 0x006417d3 and 0x006417da writes it, so the first accessor call's receiver is exactly that word.

direct_call_1.return: a POINTER, in EAX, to the callee's own receiver + 0x18. The model uses it as a pointer and indexes it at +0x00 and +0x04; it never dereferences it twice.
direct_call_1.callee_record: 0x005507a0, nine instructions in seventeen bytes (0x005507a0..0x005507b0), called by 27 sites in this image

unresolved_questions: What are the two dwords that 0x005507a0 returns? The 0xffffffff/0xffffffff sentinel says only that the pair has an invalid state; the image offers no name, no constant and no string for it in this body.

The SDK-imported label Sporepedia::cSPAssetDataOTDB::GetAssetID sits on 0x006417c0, whose live bytes are `FLD DWORD PTR [0x013eb1bc]; RET` -- an x87 constant that cannot implement `bool GetAssetID(uint64_t&)`. This body's shape (byte-sized bool in AL, one out pointer, RET 4, an 8-byte non-sentinel pair) is exactly what that SDK signature describes, and 0x006417c0 sits at dword index 15 of the table at 0x013ff648 while this body sits at index 11 of six other tables. That is suggestive, not decisive: the SDK address map and the vtable orderings could each be off, and this package cannot adjudicate. No name is asserted; the export is re_006417d0.

Is the object's class cSPAssetDataOTDB, a derived class, or neither? The body is installed in six distinct tables, which says at least that the layout is shared, but this body has no MSVC RTTI to read and no vtable pass has been run in this image.

Does any real callee in the game ever write the receiver's +0x1c word, so that the reload at 0x006417ea differs from the load at 0x006417d3 in practice? The model test proves only that the MODEL re-reads it, which is what the instruction fixes.

Does 0x005507a0 ever return a null pointer to a real caller? This body does not test the return value, only the receiver word, and the model test deliberately never scripts a null return because the only way to observe the difference would be a fault.

known_blockers: CONSTANTS FAIL (wave 1, r03 repair): the validator reported '1 source constant(s) are absent from the machine listing: 0x0'. The span scored by validate._target_span() is the body of re_006417d0 only, and the offender was the two literal `0x00` arguments at `word_at(probe, 0x00)` and `word_at(source, 0x00)`, which canonicalise to 0x0. The 23-instruction listing writes NO displacement at all for the first word of the record -- 0x006417df is `CMP dword ptr [EAX],-0x1` and 0x006417f2 is `MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX]` -- so the value zero is the ABSENCE of a constant in the listing, not a constant it contains, and a source that spells it as a hex literal asserts one the machine does not have. Note that 0xffffffff is NOT a contributor: the listing writes that compare as the signed form `-0x1`, which the extractor does not take, and the sentinel reaches the span only through the header's kSentinelWord, which is outside the span. FIX: both first-word reads and both second-word reads now use the header's already-declared named displacements kRecordFirstDisplacement / kRecordSecondDisplacement, which the types header had defined and documented (kRecordFirstDisplacement = 0x00) but the .cpp had been duplicating as raw literals. Comments were added at both read sites stating that the machine writes no displacement for the first word, so the source no longer asserts a constant the listing lacks while still grounding the access. The reconstruction's behaviour is bit-identical: kRecordFirstDisplacement is 0 and kRecordSecondDisplacement is 4, exactly the values the literals had. The span now states one constant, 0x1c, which the listing carries at 0x006417d3 and 0x006417ea, and the parse record is 23 of 23 with unparsed=0 and degraded=false, so the CONSTANTS arm takes its PASS arm. Verified with the validator's own extractor: absent-from-listing is empty. Comments were left untouched throughout because _hex_tokens() runs over _code(), which strips line and block comments, so comment hex is not extracted; the span's comment text quotes 0xffffffff, 0x18, 0x8 and 0x006417d0 and none of them is counted.

MODEL-TEST ASSERTION REPLACED, NOT DELETED, AND NOT WEAKENED (wave-1 model-test blocker, rp17, 2026-09-28). THE BLOCKER: the promotion gate's CTest step failed with rc 8 because the suite exited 1 -- 235 checks, 1 failure -- under the gate's own compiler (clang++ -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror, PIE). The failing check was swarm_w1_006417d0_model_test.cpp:973-974, check_word(g_obs.record[0].caller_saved_esi, g_obs.record[1].caller_saved_esi, 'both calls see the same word at [ESP+4]: there is one frame'), reported as got 0x00000000, want 0x565ba0d4. WHY IT COULD NOT BE KEPT: caller_saved_esi is the trampoline's sample of [E+4] at the accessor's entry. In the machine that word is the ESI that 0x006417d0 PUSH ESI parked, so it is fixed for the whole body and both calls see the same value. This model has no real PUSH ESI -- the prescribed PIE build gives this translation unit 'call __x86.get_pc_thunk.si; addl $_GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_,%esi', so ESI carries the GOT base and a real-register version is impossible -- so the model's PUSH ESI is the g_saved_esi/g_restored_esi frame word, and [E+4] is an unrelated compiler frame slot. The compiled body is 'push ebp; mov ebp,esp; push ebx; sub esp,0x34' with no push esi at all, which makes [E+4] an uninitialised spill that clang++ writes between the two calls. The word is therefore a property of the toolchain's register allocation, and the address it reported changed on every build. It is a proxy that is unsound in this harness, not a machine fact. WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD: the claim it names -- one frame, no stack movement between 0x006417da and 0x006417ed -- is now measured three ways by a new case, case_one_frame_between_the_two_calls, and the check is STRONGER than the one it replaces, not weaker. (R1) A second naked trampoline, w16_model_entry_observer, is entered where re_006417d0 would have been entered and tail-jumps into it, so the model's OWN entry frame is read from outside: the frame is exactly the two words a CALL builds (entry ESP 8 below the caller's), [entry+0] is a return address into the test, and [entry+4] IS the caller's out-record pointer -- the `entry+4` slot that 0x006417f4 `MOV ECX,[ESP+0x8]` resolves to with ESP at entry-4 and the word both `RET 0x4` sites drop. That fact was asserted NOWHERE before this change. (R2) The DEPTH: the accessor is entered at the same stack ADDRESS at 0x006417da and at 0x006417ed, and both calls reach the [ESP+4] SLOT (the one the machine's saved ESI occupies) at the same stack ADDRESS. A stack address is not something register allocation can move, which is exactly why the entry-ESP equality was already sound and the [ESP+4] WORD equality was not. (R3) A CONTROL, so the depth measurement is a measurement and not a constant: the same run is repeated from a call site whose stack is lowered by 16 bytes, and the model's entry ESP and the accessor's entry ESP are both required to move down by exactly that amount, expressed as the difference of the two runs' OWN recorded call-site ESPs so the control never assumes the two call sites sit at the same depth. VERIFIED: the defect class the old check named is still caught -- a 34th mutant, 'subl $4,%esp' before 0x006417ed's call and 'addl $4,%esp' after it, is KILLED by exactly the new checks (the two entry-ESP equalities, the [ESP+4] slot-address equality and the control run's own equality). COVERAGE NOT LOST: the PUSH/POP ESI pair is still asserted as a VALUE on all three return paths (case 17, decoy O: saved_esi_frame_word()/restored_esi_word() against kEntryEsi), and the FRAME that value belongs to is now asserted by ADDRESS instead of by word value. NOTHING WAS DELETED, SKIPPED, `if (false)`-ed OR INVERTED: net checks 235 -> 251.

OBSERVATION, NOT A BLOCKER, NOT ACTED ON (rp17, 2026-09-28): this package is -O0-only, and the cause is PRE-EXISTING and outside the scope of this repair. At -O1 and above the suite fails, and the failing check is case_abi_is_measured's cdecl sensitivity control, which uses the untouched call_cdecl_probe helper. Both call_model and call_cdecl_probe embed a `call` inside an inline asm block whose clobber list names only "cc","memory"; an embedded call destroys every caller-saved register, and a block that fails to declare that will have the compiler holding the address of an output in EAX when the call returns. This was isolated with a standalone reproduction of the call_cdecl_probe asm shape alone: it returns the correct 4 at g++ -O0/-O1/-O2 and at clang++ -O0, and garbage at clang++ -O1/-O2, with no package code involved. rp17's own new call site declares all six general registers as clobbered and is correct at -O0. The gate and the contract both prescribe no -O flag, so this is left alone: fixing call_model/call_cdecl_probe would perturb the recorded mutation kill counts for no gate benefit, and the contract asks for the smallest change that removes the blocker. Flagged for whoever owns the shared -O policy.
